headline: Scientists find air around a faraway planet

sources.title: Potential Atmosphere Detected on Habitable-Zone Exoplanet LHS 1140b
Astronomers spot first atmosphere around a potentially habitable alien world
Rocky Planet 48 Light-Years Away May Be First in a Habitable Zone With a Confirmed Atmosphere
Atmosphere Confirmed Around Habitable Zone Planet LHS 1140b (video, Anton Petrov)

chunks.text: Scientists have {{picked up}} the first signs of air around a small, rocky planet outside our [[solar system]]. The planet, called LHS 1140 b, sits about 48 [[light-years]] from Earth. It circles its star in the zone where the temperature could be right for water. This is [[a huge deal]], because a planet needs air to {{hold on to}} heat and to give life a chance. But the discovery did not {{end up}} being simple.

chunks.text: LHS 1140 b is a [[super-Earth]], which means it is rocky like Earth but much bigger. To study it, a team at Harvard University {{set out}} to watch the planet with a powerful [[telescope]] in Chile. In 2024, they {{came across}} [[helium]] [[gas]] escaping from the top of the planet's air. The planet's star {{gives off}} strong [[radiation]], and this slowly {{strips away}} the gas. For the scientists, it was a rare [[privilege]] to [[witness]] this so far from Earth.

chunks.text: In a surprising [[twist]], the [[signal]] did not last. When the team {{went back}} to check the planet in 2025, the helium had completely disappeared. Scientists think the air may [[shift]] and change over time, which is why the signal appeared and then [[vanished]]. For now, the change is a [[mystery]]. The team is not [[certain]] what happened, and more work is needed to {{find out}} what is {{going on}}.

chunks.text: To {{clear up}} the mystery, the team will {{take on}} a bigger study with the James Webb Space Telescope, the most powerful space telescope ever built. Their main goal is to {{track down}} water, which would [[prove]] the air is real. If they {{pull off}} this hard job and [[succeed]], LHS 1140 b could become one of the best places to look for life. Scientists around the world will follow the results closely.

mainIdea.s: Scientists picked up signs of air on a distant rocky planet, but the signal vanished when they went back to check. They now plan a bigger study to find out if real air is there.
mainIdea.why: The team found helium escaping from the planet in 2024, but the signal had vanished by 2025. They now plan a bigger study with a powerful telescope to track down water.

mainIdea.s: Scientists have proven that a distant rocky planet holds a stable layer of air that can support life. Their next step, they say, is only to learn more about the planet's size and shape.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the article never says the air was proven or stable. The helium signal disappeared, and the team is not certain what happened.

mainIdea.s: Astronomers announced this year that they found a brand new rocky planet in a far off solar system. Thick clouds and intense heat make this new world a poor place to search for life.
mainIdea.why: This is about a different planet and a different discovery. The real story is about LHS 1140 b and a helium signal that appeared and then vanished.
